clue.text: House repeatedly cut short Santa's little outburst

parts.note: HO is the short form of house, as in addresses
repeatedly means the same short form given again, here twice more

explanation.surface: Father Christmas lets out a little exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' tells you to use the abbreviation of house rather than the full word.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Claus is traditionally given a jolly triple chuckle as his catchphrase laugh.

clue.text: Not the royal family's favourite programme of late, that's the broad view

definitions.text: Not the royal family's favourite programme of late
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the BBC current affairs programme that broadcast Princess Diana's 1995 interview
second meaning: a wide unbroken view of an area

explanation.walkthrough: In November 1995 Panorama aired Diana's interview about her failing marriage, to the royal family's dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is an uninterrupted sweeping vista, and also the name of the long-running BBC documentary series.

clue.text: Carol's orgasmic invitation to a political party rally?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Christmas carol of that name; the 's reads as is, joining the two meanings

definitions.text: orgasmic invitation to a political party rally
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a cry of pleasure followed by a summons to all the party loyalists

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name, which makes the rest sound like her bedroom cry; it is the Christmas hymn, whose opening words also read as a call to the party faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christmas hymn begins with an invitation to the loyal believers, here read as summoning a party's loyal supporters.

clue.text: Go-getting Di — many upsets with Charles at first

indicators.note: upsets means knocks over, so the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: the word Charles, whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: The Princess of Wales, energetic, upsets many people, Charles above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes C from Charles; 'with' joins it to DI and MANY, and 'upsets' rearranges the whole lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamic person is energetic and ambitious, someone who drives ahead to achieve things.

clue.text: To be right next to an arse, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: an arse is a butt, said as a butt

explanation.surface: Someone stands uncomfortably close to a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to adjoin or share a border with something.

clue.text: Get high, like, on Conservative downfall

parts.note: like means as, in comparison
one's downfall is one's end

explanation.surface: A druggy teenager's remark about the Tories' collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins AS to what follows. 'Get high' reads as taking drugs but means climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to rise or climb upward.

clue.text: A big knob is highly regarded by Catholics

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an important person, or a raised piece of ground
second meaning: Your ... is the title of a Catholic cardinal

explanation.walkthrough: 'is' joins the two meanings. 'big knob' is slang for a bigwig.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminence is a person of high rank and also a rising hillock; cardinals are addressed by the title.

clue.text: Norma's upset by Conservative gutless hierarchy, as a rule

indicators.note: Norma is upset, overturned, so her letters are scrambled

parts.note: the name Norma; the 's is read as is

indicators.note: gutless means the insides are removed, keeping only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Norma, perhaps a Tory wife, is dismayed by a spineless party establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: NORMA rearranged is MONAR, then C, then HY from hierarchy without its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy is a form of rule by a king or queen.

clue.text: A couple of tits see the point in Big Bang

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the word for a big bang

parts.note: a boom is a loud explosive noise
S, south, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of birdwatching interrupted by an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the compass point inside the big bang; 'see' only joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosom is a woman's chest, the pair of breasts, which slang calls tits.

clue.text: Pub crowded — so a stable environment for delivery had to found

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a full public house has no space left

definitions.text: a stable environment for delivery had to found
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the reason in the Nativity story that a stable had to be found for Mary to give birth

explanation.walkthrough: 'so' joins the two meanings, and the clue reads 'had to [be] found'. 'delivery' is childbirth and the 'stable environment' is the Bethlehem stable, not a calm setting.
explanation.definitionFit: In Luke's gospel Jesus was laid in a manger because there was no space for the family in the lodging house.

clue.text: See 10
One has to act badly with nothing on back in the USA

indicators.note: back here means the assembled string of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: one is A, as in a single thing
to ham is to overact
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A performer forced to act terribly with no clothes on, somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to', 'with' and 'on' string the pieces together in order, and 'back' turns the whole string round.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is a city in Nebraska, so it is a place found in the United States.

clue.text: Not wishing to be seen to be like Salman Rushdie?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: keeping out of sight, concealed
second meaning: the novelist lived concealed under police protection after the 1989 fatwa

explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' joins the two meanings; the surface reads as someone avoiding comparison with the author.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keeping out of sight in a secret place is concealed, as the novelist was for years after the fatwa.

clue.text: See 27
Is able to be twisted inside bloke as a means of stopping hands wandering!

definitions.text: a means of stopping hands wandering

indicators.note: inside places the turned-round letters within the word for bloke

parts.note: a bloke is a male

indicators.note: twisted means turned round, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: is able means can

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about restraining a man whose hands roam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is able' is the verb can; 'twisted' reads it backwards as NAC and 'inside' sets that within the word for a man. The exclamation mark flags the saucy surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A manacle is a metal shackle for the wrists, which keeps a person's hands restrained.

clue.text: Crown in the grip of one single mobster

indicators.note: in the grip of means held inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: alone, read as A LONE: one single person
to cap something is to crown it, the top of it

explanation.surface: A crown clutched by a lone gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one single' is read as A LONE, and 'in the grip of' puts CAP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era.

clue.text: Made a balls-up of gobbling Labour's leader — OYLE gagged

indicators.note: gobbling means swallowing, so the first word takes in the letter

parts.note: to muff something is to bungle it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word Labour, whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone botched things by swallowing the party leader and was silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes L from Labour, and 'gobbling' has MUFFED swallow it. The stray OYLE in the printed clue plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Muffled means having the sound deadened or covered, like a person who has been gagged.

clue.text: See 3
Devious little Colonel North taking in stupid nit of a president

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the second jumble goes into the first
devious means twisting, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: COL is the short form of Colonel

indicators.note: stupid suggests muddled, so the three letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Oliver North, of the Iran-Contra affair, as a scheming soldier dealing with a foolish president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devious' jumbles COL and N into CLON, 'stupid' jumbles NIT into INT, and 'taking in' puts INT into CLON.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton was the President of the United States at the time.

clue.text: Tory Gale's pissed — clot!

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory

indicators.note: pissed is slang for drunk, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Gale's reads as Gale is: the name that gets jumbled

explanation.surface: An insult at a drunken Conservative called Gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pissed' rearranges GALE into GEAL. 'clot' looks like the insult that caps the surface, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To congeal is to thicken from liquid to a semi-solid, which is what blood does when it clots.

clue.text: Arrested Leeson and Ian Hislop

parts.note: Nick Leeson, the rogue trader who broke Barings Bank and was arrested in 1995
Hislop is editor of Private Eye, where this puzzle ran; ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A joke that the rogue trader and the magazine's editor were both arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicked is British slang for arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicked is informal British slang for taken in by police.

clue.text: The mess surrounding would-be ambassador, a familiar odd-ball dame!

indicators.note: surrounding places the jumbled letters around the short name
a mess is a jumble, so these three letters are rearranged

parts.note: Diana, Princess of Wales, said she wanted to be an ambassador for Britain

explanation.surface: A scene of eccentric dames around a princess who fancied a diplomatic role.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Diana said she wanted to be a roving ambassador for Britain. 'mess' jumbles the three-letter word into ETH and 'surrounding' wraps that round her short name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Edith Sitwell was a famously eccentric poet, and her first name is the familiar form.

clue.text: Straight up the nose, maybe, but not Ecstasy

indicators.note: up as in stirred up: the letters are shaken into a new order
but not means one letter is left out of the shuffled letters

parts.note: E is the drug slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Sniffing cocaine is fine, but no pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straight up the nose' reads as snorting a drug. 'but not' drops one E from THE NOSE, and 'up' rearranges the rest; 'maybe' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight is slang for truthful and fair dealing, as an honest person is.

clue.text: Piss taken by medical staff?

parts.note: taking the piss means mocking, but doctors take urine samples

explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the piss' is British slang for mocking someone; read literally, nurses collect urine for testing.
explanation.definitionFit: A urine sample handed in for laboratory testing is called a specimen.

clue.text: Smart move dumping a mate of Denis's

indicators.note: move signals that the letters are moved around into a new order
dumping means one letter is thrown out of the shuffled set

explanation.surface: A clever ploy that drops a friend of Denis Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumping' takes A out of SMART and 'move' rearranges what is left; 'Smart move' looks like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs T is Margaret Thatcher, wife of Denis Thatcher; mate is used here in the sense of spouse.

clue.text: One-time women-only second city

parts.note: one is A
a hen party or hen night is for women only

explanation.surface: A place that once barred men, now the second city of somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second city' looks like a phrase, but 'second' gives S and only 'city' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital of Greece, a famous ancient metropolis.

clue.text: Christmases at Windsor, perhaps, do make dire weekend viewing

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas, so Noels are Christmases
a do held at a country house such as Windsor Castle is a house party

explanation.surface: Royal Christmases make for grim Saturday television.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel's House Party was Noel Edmonds's Saturday-night BBC show in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: The programme was a Saturday-evening television show that the setter considers awful.

clue.text: Tantrum results from having revealed you're gay with rupture

parts.note: to be out is to have come out as gay
a burst is a rupture or split

explanation.surface: Coming out leads to a family row.
explanation.definitionFit: An outburst is a sudden fit of temper or anger.
